holidays.name: National Rice Pudding Day
holidays.description: A day to dig into a creamy, comforting bowl of rice pudding. Eat it warm with cinnamon, chilled with raisins, or dressed up with fruit or caramel. Leftover rice gets a glow-up.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It has become a regular fixture on August calendars for dessert lovers.
holidays.funFact: Versions of rice pudding show up all over the world, from Indian kheer to Spanish arroz con leche, and it is often made from leftover rice.

holidays.name: National Book Lovers Day
holidays.description: A day for bookworms to ignore their to-do lists, find a cozy spot, and finish a chapter, or the whole book. Browse a bookstore, swap favorites with a friend, or just reread an old classic.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It has grown in popularity as readers share their favorite books and reading nooks online.
holidays.funFact: The word 'bibliophile' for a book lover comes from Greek roots meaning 'book' and 'loving'.

holidays.name: National Hand-Holding Day
holidays.description: A sweet and simple day for taking someone's hand, whether it's a partner, a kid, a friend, or a grandparent. It costs nothing and takes no preparation.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It is listed on August 9 alongside other lighthearted days.
holidays.funFact: Studies have suggested that holding hands with someone you trust can help calm stress responses and may even ease the perception of pain.
